notifyOnModificationOfAnElement.description: Notify on modification/deletion of an element. The observed elements are the ones ACAPI_Element_GetElemList returns, for API_ZombieElemID or, with elementTypesToObserve, for each of those types, when the first client asking for these notifications of them is registered, and every element of the observed types created after that. Archicad does not report the changes made by Tapir's own commands, so Tapir reports them itself for SetDetailsOfElements, SetPropertyValuesOfElements, MoveElements, RotateElements, MirrorElements (not for the copies they make, which are new elements), DeleteElements, DeleteSelectedElements, the Modify<Tool> commands (ModifyWalls, ModifyBeams, ModifySlabs, ModifyColumns, ModifyWindows, ModifyDoors, ModifyOpenings, ModifyMorphs, ModifyRoofs, ModifyShells, ModifyMeshes, ModifyObjects, ModifyLamps, ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels, ModifyCurtainWalls, ModifyCurtainWallFrames, ModifyZones, ModifySections, ModifyDetailMarkers, ModifyRailings, ModifyStairs), ChangeTextContent, SetGDLParametersOfElements, RunParameterScriptOfElements (only when the script changed the element), SetMarkerParametersOfElements, SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements, ChangeLibraryPartOfElements, SetClassificationsOfElements, SetCategoryValuesOfElements, ModifyPropertyValueOfElements, SetElementInfoStrings, SetURLReferencesOfElements, SetIFCAttributesOfElements, SetIFCPropertiesOfElements, RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements, SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, LockElements, UnlockElements, SetOpeningDetails, SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, SetOpeningSymbolParameters, CreateGroups and UngroupElements (the grouped elements), MoveElementsToDesignOptions, CreateSolidElementLinks, RemoveSolidElementLinks, CreateSolidOperations (the target and operator when the operation changed or deleted them; the results are new elements), TrimElements, RemoveElementTrims, MergeElements, UnmergeElements, ModifyMEPRoutingElements, ModifyMEPPorts (the element owning the port), ConnectMEPElements, ModifyMEPElements, SetMEPRoutingParameters, ModifyElectricalPanels, ModifyElectricalDevices and ConnectToElectricalCircuits. Of the elements these commands change, only the given ones are reported: an element deleted together with its owner (a door or window of a deleted wall) is not. UpdateZones is not reported by Tapir, because Archicad updates the Zones after the command has returned. When the user moves, rotates, mirrors, elevates, resizes or stretches elements in Archicad, each of their changedElements items also has a transformation: {"type": ..., ...}, where type is "Drag" (with displacement: {"x", "y", "z"}), "Elevate" (with displacement, only z is not 0), "Rotate" (with origin: {"x", "y"} and angle, in radians, counterclockwise), "Mirror" (with origin, a point of the mirror axis, and axisDirection: {"x", "y"}, its unit vector), "Resize" (with origin and ratio), "Stretch", "VerticalStretch", "PreservedHeightStretch", "PreservedDirectionStretch" or "General"; the changes made by Tapir's own commands and by undo or redo have no transformation. Optional parameter, by default true. Archicad attaches an observer to each element to observe (see elementTypesToObserve) when the first client asks for this, and detaches them when the last one stops, and it is blocked meanwhile: the time grows faster than the number of elements, from seconds for a few hundred elements to many minutes for a few thousand. Count the elements first (GetAllElements with IncludeSubElemObjects, or GetElementsByType) and limit the types on large projects.

elementTypesToObserve.description: Only modifications/deletions of elements of these types are observed and notified to this client. Optional parameter, by default every element (including the parts of curtain walls, stairs and railings, which are most of the elements of large projects). Registering the same client again with other types changes them; only the elements of types no client observed before get an observer then. Does not limit the other notifications.

notifyOnReservationChanges.description: Notify on reservation changes of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.

notifyOnSelectionChange.description: Notify when the selection changes. The message is {"selectedElements": [...]}: the whole current selection, each item an elementId as in the response of GetSelectedElements, an empty list when nothing is selected. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnWindowChange.description: Notify when the current (active) window changes or the user switches to another story. The message is {"windowChanged": {"event": "Window" or "Floor", "windowType": ..., "databaseId": ..., "storyIndex": ...}}: windowType and databaseId describe the new current window as in the response of GetCurrentWindowType (databaseId is missing when that response has none), storyIndex is the active story, missing when it cannot be read. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnProjectEvents.description: Notify on project events. The message is {"projectEvent": ...}, one of "New", "NewAndReset", "Open", "Close", "Quit", "SendChanges" (a Teamwork send is about to start) and "ReceiveChanges" (Teamwork changes were received). The client stays registered when the project is closed or another one is opened. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnAttributeReplacement.description: Notify when attributes are deleted and replaced by other attributes of the same type (for example Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager). The message is {"replacedAttributes": [{"attributeType": ..., "oldIndex": ..., "newIndex": ..., "newAttributeId": ...}, ...]}: attributeType is one of the type names of GetAttributesByType ("Layer", "Line", "Fill", "Composite", "Surface", "LayerCombination", "ZoneCategory", "Profile", "PenTable", "MEPSystem", "OperationProfile", "BuildingMaterial", or "Unknown"), oldIndex is the index of the replaced attribute and newIndex the index of the attribute that replaces it, newAttributeId is the attributeId of that attribute, missing when it cannot be found. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnToolChange.description: Notify when the user switches to another tool in the Toolbox. The message is {"toolChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type of the new tool, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), "None" for the Arrow and the Marquee, and "Unknown" for a tool Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnViewEvents.description: Notify when an item of the Project Navigator or the Organizer is inserted (for example a view is saved or a layout is created), modified (for example renamed), deleted or opened. The message is {"viewEvent": {"event": ..., "navigatorMapId": ..., "navigatorItemId": {"guid": ...}}}: event is one of "Inserted", "Modified", "Deleted" and "Opened", navigatorMapId is the navigator map of the item, one of "ProjectMap", "PublicViewMap", "MyViewMap", "LayoutBook" and "PublisherSets" (as navigatorMapId of GetNavigatorItemTree), and navigatorItemId is the guid of the navigator item, as in the response of GetNavigatorItemTree (a deleted item no longer exists). Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnLockableReservationChanges.description: Notify when a Teamwork lockable object set (the non-element things Teamwork reserves: the attributes of a type, favorites, model view options, project info, project preferences, ...) is reserved or released, by anyone, including the current user. The message is {"lockableReservationChanged": {"event": ..., "objectSetId": {"guid": ...}, "objectSetName": ..., "reservedBy": ..., "reservedByUserId": ...}}: event is "Reserved" or "Released", objectSetId is the guid of the object set, objectSetName its name as objectSetName of ReserveLockableObjectSet (for example "Composites", "LayerSettingsDialog" or "Favorites"), missing when it is not one of the documented sets, and reservedBy and reservedByUserId are the name and the Teamwork user id of the member who reserved it, only for "Reserved". Element reservations are notified by notifyOnReservationChanges. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnToolDefaultChanges.description: Notify when the default settings of a tool change (for example the user changes the settings of the Wall tool with no wall selected), so a client can read the new defaults. The message is {"toolDefaultsChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type whose defaults changed, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), and "Unknown" for a type Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnAttributeChanges.description: Notify when attributes (layers, fills, composites, surfaces, building materials, ...) are created, modified or deleted. The message is {"attributesChanged": {"event": ..., "attributeIds": [{"attributeId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and attributeIds are the attributes, as in the response of GetAttributesByType (a deleted attribute no longer exists). Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnClassificationChanges.description: Notify when classification systems or classification items are created, modified or deleted. The messages are {"classificationSystemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationSystemIds": [{"classificationSystemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"classificationItemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationItemIds": [{"classificationItemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllClassificationSystems and GetAllClassificationsInSystem. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnPropertyDefinitionChanges.description: Notify when property groups or property definitions are created, modified or deleted (property values of elements are notified as changedElements by notifyOnModificationOfAnElement). The messages are {"propertyGroupsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyGroupIds": [{"propertyGroupId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"propertyDefinitionsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyIds": [{"propertyId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllProperties. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOnMarqueeChange.description: Notify when the marquee is drawn, changed or removed. The message is {"marqueeChanged": {"type": ..., "multiStory": ...}}: type is "rectangle", "rotatedRectangle", "polygon" or, when the marquee was removed, "none", as type of GetMarquee, which returns the shape of the marquee; multiStory is missing for "none". Available from Archicad 27: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

notifyOn3DSettingsChanges.description: Notify when the settings of the 3D window change (projection, Filter and Cut Elements in 3D, 3D window settings). The message is {"view3DSettingsChanged": {}}; read the new settings with the commands of the 3D window. The changes made while navigating in 3D are not notified. Available from Archicad 30: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.

elementUserData.description: The elements with the key-value pairs to store on them. Each item needs userData, keysToDelete or both.

executionResults.description: One result per input item, in the input order.

date.description: The date GDL scripts should see, in the format GetGDLDate returns.

index.description: The index of the parameter.

index1.description: Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.

index2.description: Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.

value.description: The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

index1.description: Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.

index2.description: Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.

value.description: The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

elementsWithGDLParameters.description: The elements with GDL parameters dictionary pairs.

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementsWithGDLParameters, in the order of the input. On a dry run the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, but the element is not changed. An element that passes every check made before changing it (the element and its parameters exist, every value is valid for its parameter, the element is editable) gets wouldChange: oldValue and newValue list the parameters a real run would change - the ones given and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them - before and after, each with name, index, type and value as GetGDLParametersOfElements gives them. Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

SetGhostStorySettingsParameters.description: Every field is optional; the ones left out keep their current value. A story choice (showOne, showAbove or showBelow true) replaces the current reference, whatever it is; without one the reference is kept, also when it is another view (a section, an elevation, a worksheet).

on.description: Show (true) or hide (false) the ghost story on the floor plan.

showOne.description: Show the story at storyIndex as the ghost story.

showAbove.description: Show the story above the current one as the ghost story.

showBelow.description: Show the story below the current one as the ghost story.

storyIndex.description: The index of the story to show when showOne is true, as GetStories reports it.

ghostColor.description: The color to draw the ghost story in.

filter.description: The element types to show in the ghost story; the others are hidden.

ruleGroupNames.description: The names of the rule groups in their new order. The groups not listed keep their order and follow the listed ones.

graphicOverrideRuleGroups.description: The rule groups to reorder, in the shape GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups returns them.

hotlinkInstances.description: The placed hotlink instances to change the design option table of. Every field but elementId is optional; what is omitted keeps its current value. The changes are applied in the order filterMode, activeDesignOptionCombination, activeDesignOptions.

elementIFCAttributeValues.description: The IFC attribute values to set.

elementIFCClassificationReferences.description: The IFC classification references to store on the elements.

elementIFCPropertyValues.description: The IFC property values to set. Only single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties are supported.

elementTypes.description: The element types to set the last 3D default level of.

levels.description: The new last 3D default level of each element type, in the order of elementTypes, in meters.

layersOfElementDefaults.description: The element types whose tool defaults get a new layer.

layerId.description: The layer new elements of this type will be placed on.

executionResults.description: One result per item, in the input order.

libraries.description: Local library folders or container files, by absolute path.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

sectionId.description: The type identifier of the custom section. A four-character code is given as its integer value, the first character in the highest byte (e.g. 'ABCD' is 1094861636).

index.description: Optional. The index of the section among the sections with the same identifier. By default 0.

dataVersion.description: Optional. The data version stored with the section. By default 0. Only used with data.

data.description: The new content of the section, base64 encoded. The section is created when it does not exist, otherwise replaced. Give either data or delete.

delete.description: When true, the section is deleted. Give either data or delete.

libraryParts.description: The library parts to modify and the metadata to set in each.
The library parts to modify and the parameter values to set in each.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

previewPicture.description: Optional. The new preview picture as a base64 encoded PNG.

gdlPictures.description: Optional. The new GDL pictures, each a base64 encoded PNG. They replace all GDL pictures of the library part.

darkPreviewPicture.description: Optional. The new preview picture for the dark user interface as a base64 encoded PNG. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

darkGdlPictures.description: Optional. The new GDL pictures for the dark user interface, each a base64 encoded PNG. They replace all dark GDL pictures of the library part. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

name.description: The name of the loaded library part file with its extension, as returned in the fileName field of GetAvailableLibraryParts (e.g. 'My Door.gsm').

deletePreviewPicture.description: Optional. When true, the preview picture is deleted.

deleteDarkPreviewPicture.description: Optional. When true, the preview picture for the dark user interface is deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

deleteGdlPictures.description: Optional. When true, all GDL pictures are deleted.

deleteDarkGdlPictures.description: Optional. When true, all GDL pictures for the dark user interface are deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or newer.

copy2DSymbolFrom.description: Optional. The name of another loaded library part (fileName with extension); its 2D symbol (the drawn 2D vector image) replaces this part's 2D symbol.

delete2DSymbol.description: Optional. When true, the 2D symbol (the drawn 2D vector image) is deleted. Cannot be combined with copy2DSymbolFrom.

libraryParts.description: The library parts to modify, with the scripts to set and to delete in each.

elementsWithLinkedPropertyObjects.description: The property object links to set, each for an element or for the element defaults of an element type. A link that is not given stays unchanged.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

rows.description: The rows to change. Only the given values are set.

executionResults.description: One result per row, in the order of the rows.

elements.description: The routing parameters to change. Only the given keys are changed. An item gives either routingNodeParameters and/or routingSegmentParameters for a routing element, or elbowParameters and/or transitionParameters for a routing node.

elementsWithMarkerLibraryPart.description: The elements with the library part their marker should use.

libraryPartName.description: The name of the library part the marker should use, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements and GetAvailableLibraryParts report it. It has to be a marker library part: Archicad's marker parent for windows or doors, or a library part derived from it. Any other library part is refused.

elementsWithMarkerParameters.description: The elements with the marker parameters to change.

polygon.description: The vertices of a polygon marquee, in order. The polygon is closed automatically; a repeated first vertex at the end is accepted. Give either polygon or box.

box.description: A rectangle marquee. With rotationAngle it is a rotated rectangle, and the box is read the way Archicad stores it (see GetMarquee): in the coordinate system rotated by rotationAngle around the project origin. Give either polygon or box.

rotationAngle.description: Rotation angle (radians) of the box around the project origin. Only together with box. The default is 0: a horizontal rectangle.

multiStory.description: True for a multi-story (thick) marquee, false for a single-story (thin) one. The default is false.

extrusionParameters.description: The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.

floorPlanParameters.description: The floor plan settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. The ones left out are not changed.

elementType.description: The type of the elements the changed settings are the defaults of.

openingsWithDetails.description: The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to change, each with the details to set. A detail that is left out stays as it is.

pens.description: The pens to change among the pens in effect in the current window, the ones GetPens returns. Only the given fields (color, width, description) of a listed pen are changed.

values.description: The project data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

projectInfoId.description: The id of the project info field.

projectInfoValue.description: The new value of the project info field. An empty string clears the field.

architect.description: Architect: the full name of the Project Info contact. Archicad keeps it as name parts (title prefix, given, middle and family name, title suffix); SetProjectNotes puts a new value into the given name and clears the other parts, so it reads back unchanged. Use SetProjectInfoField to set the parts.

draftsmen.description: Draftsmen: the full name of the Project Info CAD technician, kept as name parts like architect.

dateOfIssue.description: Date of issue (free text, as typed in Project Notes).

SetProjectPreferencesParameters.description: The pages to change, by name. Only the given fields of a page change, the rest keeps its value. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set has to be reserved first (ReserveLockableObjectSet).

SetProjectPreferencesResult.description: One execution result per page given in the input, by name.

attributeIds.description: The attributes to set the value on. The property must be available for every one of them.

elementDefaultPropertyValues.description: The property values to set on the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of element types.

items.description: A property value with the identifier of the property and the element type whose defaults own it.

elementPropertyValues.description: A single real value accepts '.' or ',' as the decimal separator, so the value strings GetPropertyValuesOfElements returns can be written back: when both appear the last one is the decimal separator, a separator that appears more than once groups thousands, and a single separator is the decimal one. Unitless real and integer lists accept semicolon-separated numbers; an empty string sets an empty list. Invalid items reject the entire property write.

executionResults.description: One result for each item of elementPropertyValues, in the order of the input. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the property values of the element can be read, the value is editable for the element and converts to the property's type) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's value now as GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives it (left out when the property is not available or not evaluated for the element), newValue the value that would be written in the same format (left out for valueStatus Default). Archicad can still refuse a value that passes them.

suspendGroups.description: Turn the Suspend Groups mode on or off.

elementsWithURLReferences.description: The elements and the web link to set on each.

pairs.description: The key-value pairs to store on each attribute. A key the attribute already holds gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

executionResults.description: One result per attribute, in the input order.

groups.description: The groups to store the pairs on.

pairs.description: The key-value pairs to store on each group. A key the group already holds gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

executionResults.description: One result per group, in the input order.

modelViewOptionIndex.description: Switches the window to the model view option combination with this index, as GetViewOptions, FindModelViewOption and GetModelViewOptionDetails return it. Archicad then applies the model view options stored in the combination: viewOptions.modelViewOptions are not applied together with an index, viewOptions.onScreenViewOptions are. Archicad may renumber the combinations when the view options of a window change, so look the index up by name with FindModelViewOption right before switching.

automaticLabeling.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones (placing a Label on each new Zone) on or off.

favoriteName.description: The name of the Label Favorite that is placed on each new Zone by the automatic labeling.

zoomBox.description: The area to zoom the current 2D window to, in model coordinates (meters). The window keeps its aspect ratio, so the shown area may be larger than the box. The rotation of the window is kept as it is.

ShellBaseFloorFill.description: Floor plan cover fill settings of a Roof or Shell (API_ShellBaseType).

use.description: Whether the cover fill is shown on the floor plan.

use3DHatching.description: Use the fill of the surface material (Vectorial 3D Hatch) as the cover fill.

useFillLocBaseLine.description: Align the cover fill with the pivot line instead of the fill handle.

useSlantedFill.description: Distort the cover fill to show the slope as seen from above.

ShellCutBodyType.description: How the body is extended for connections (Model panel). A shell uses Editable, UpwardsExtrusion or DownwardsExtrusion.

ShellCutPolygon.description: A closed polygon cutting a shell: its clipping contour or a hole.

coordinates.description: The points of the polygon, in the XY plane of 'plane'.

arcs.description: Arc segments of the polygon, with indices into coordinates.

plane.description: The plane of the polygon, in the coordinates of the shell's base plane: a hole is extruded from it along its Z axis. The base plane itself by default.

depth.description: Required for holes, ignored for the clipping contour: how far the cutting body is extruded from the polygon's plane, along its Z axis (negative values cut downwards).

ShellData.description: The parameters of the new Shell.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Shell favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

shellClass.description: Extruded: 'profile' swept along 'extrusionVector'. Revolved: 'profile' turned around 'axis'. Ruled: a surface ruled between 'profile' and 'secondProfile'.

floorIndex.description: Optional story index of the shell. Without it the shell is placed on the story of the Shell tool defaults.

basePlane.description: Base plane of the shell, in project coordinates; the profiles, the extrusion, the axis and the contour and hole polygons are given in it. The project axes by default, except for a Revolved shell, whose default base plane stands upright (its Y axis is the project Z axis), so the profile's x is the radius and its y the height.

profile.description: The profile polyline. Extruded: in the plane across the extrusion, x horizontal and y up. Revolved: in the base plane's XY plane. Ruled: in the XY plane of 'profilePlane'.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic shell; a Composite shell takes its thickness from the composite.

isFlipped.description: Applies the thickness to the other side of the reference surface.

extrusionVector.description: Extruded only, required: the direction and length of the extrusion, in base plane coordinates.

extrusionStart.description: Extruded only: the point the extrusion starts from, in base plane coordinates.

shapePlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the profile's plane, in radians.

begPlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the start plane of the extrusion, in radians.

endPlaneTilt.description: Extruded only: tilt of the end plane of the extrusion, in radians.

slantAngle.description: Extruded and Revolved: slant of the extrusion vector or of the profile, in radians.

axis.description: Revolved only: the coordinate system whose Z axis the profile is turned around, in base plane coordinates. By default the base plane's Y axis.

revolutionAngle.description: Revolved only: the angle the profile is turned through, in radians. 2*pi (a full turn) by default.

beginAngle.description: Revolved only: the angle the revolution starts at, in radians.

distortionAngle.description: Revolved only: shear of the revolution, in radians. pi/2 (no shear) by default.

segmentsByCircle.description: Revolved only: the number of segments a full circle is resolved into.

secondProfile.description: Ruled only, required: the second profile polyline, in the XY plane of 'secondProfilePlane'.

profilePlane.description: Ruled only, required: the plane of 'profile', in base plane coordinates.

secondProfilePlane.description: Ruled only, required: the plane of 'secondProfile', in base plane coordinates.

morphingRule.description: Ruled only: how the two profiles are joined, segment by segment (Paired) or smoothly.

contour.description: Optional clipping contour: only the part of the shell inside this polygon, seen along the Z axis of its plane, is kept. Its 'depth' is ignored.

holes.description: Optional holes, each requiring 'depth' to extrude its cutting polygon along the Z axis of its plane.

begShapeEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the profile's edges at the start of the shell (the start plane of an extrusion, the begin angle of a revolution, the first profile of a ruled shell). Perpendicular at pi/2 by default, as the Shell tool draws it, also when favoriteName is given.

endShapeEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the profile's edges at the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

begSideEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the edge that the profile's first point sweeps from the start to the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

endSideEdgeTrim.description: Optional trim of the edge that the profile's last point sweeps. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true, Archicad recomputes the story visibility automatically from the shell's vertical extent.

visibility.description: The stories the shell's contour is shown on (API_ShellBaseType::visibilityCont).

fillVisibility.description: The stories the shell's cover fill is shown on (API_ShellBaseType::visibilityFill).

sectionContourPen.description: Pen of the contour of the cut surfaces (API_ShellBaseType::sectContPen).

sectionContourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the contour of the cut surfaces (API_ShellBaseType::sectContLtype).

contourPen.description: Pen of the shell's uncut contour on the floor plan (API_ShellBaseType::pen).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the shell's uncut contour on the floor plan (API_ShellBaseType::ltypeInd).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

ShellEdgeTrim.description: How a shell edge is cut.

trimType.description: Vertical, Perpendicular or Horizontal to the shell, or at 'angle' (CustomAngle).

angle.description: The trim angle in radians. Only CustomAngle uses it; pi/2 by default.

ShellProfile.description: A profile polyline of a shell, in the XY plane of its coordinate system.

arcs.description: Arc segments of the polyline, with indices into coordinates; index len(coordinates) is the first point again, which closes the polyline.

closed.description: Whether the segment from the last point back to the first one is part of the profile. False by default.

ShellQuantities.description: Quantities of a Shell element, as calculated by Archicad. Lengths in meters, areas in square meters, volumes in cubic meters.

volumeConditional.description: Conditional net volume of the shell.

referenceSurface.description: Net area of the reference surface.

oppositeSurface.description: Net area of the surface opposite to the reference.

referenceSurfaceConditional.description: Conditional area of the reference surface.

oppositeSurfaceConditional.description: Conditional area of the opposite surface.

grossReferenceSurface.description: Gross area of the reference surface.

grossOppositeSurface.description: Gross area of the opposite surface.

floorPlanArea.description: Projected floor plan area of the contour polygon.

alertType.description: The type of the alert dialog.

title.description: The title of the alert dialog.

subMessage.description: Optional smaller sub-message text below the main message.

button2.description: Label for the second button (e.g. Cancel).

button3.description: Label for the optional third button.

clickedButton.description: Index of the button the user clicked: 1 = button1, 2 = button2, 3 = button3.

elements.description: The elements to show in 3D. They become the selection, replacing the current one. Missing or empty: every element is shown, as Show All in 3D does.

navigatorItemId.description: Optional: the view (an item of the View Map) the dialog starts with.

translatorName.description: Optional: the name of the IFC export translator the dialog starts with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them.

cancelled.description: True when the user closed the dialog with Cancel; then no other field is given.

viewName.description: The name of the chosen view, when Archicad finds it in the navigator.

translatorName.description: The name of the IFC export translator the user chose, as IFCFileOperation's translatorName takes it.

message.description: The text of the notification bubble.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: How long the bubble stays, in milliseconds. Default: Archicad's default, 1000 (1 second).

coordinate.description: The model coordinate in the current database (meters) where the bubble is shown, converted like ModelToScreen does: in a 3D window it is projected with the current camera, in other windows z is disregarded. Do not give it together with screenPoint. When neither is given, the bubble is shown at the center of the current view in 2D windows and at the project's local origin otherwise.

redrawCountLimit.description: Shows the bubble at most this many times. After that it does not appear again, for any later ShowNotificationBubble call, until the user runs the 'Enable all informational messages' command in Archicad. Not set by default.

disabled.description: True turns the bubble off instead of showing it: it does not appear again, for any later ShowNotificationBubble call, until the user runs the 'Enable all informational messages' command in Archicad. False (the default) changes nothing.

ShowNotificationBubbleResult.description: The settings of the bubble after the call, read back from Archicad.

text.description: The text of the bubble. Missing when it has none.

largeIcon.description: The icon shown when the "Use large alert cues" option is on in Work Environment.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: How long the bubble stays, in milliseconds.

redrawCountLimit.description: How many times the bubble is shown at most. Missing when it has no limit.

htmlContent.description: The full HTML document to display in the Script UI palette.

width.description: Optional palette client width in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

height.description: Optional palette client height in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

title.description: Optional palette window title. Leave unset to keep the current title.

resizable.description: Whether the user can drag-resize the palette. Defaults to true.

zoomEnabled.description: Whether Ctrl+scroll/pinch zooming is allowed in the page. Defaults to true.

zoomLevel.description: Optional initial zoom level (1.0 = 100%). Leave unset to keep the current zoom.

scrollBarsVisible.description: Whether the browser's own scrollbars are shown. Defaults to true.

contextMenuEnabled.description: Whether right-click shows the browser's context menu (e.g. Inspect Element). Defaults to true.

navigationDisabled.description: Prevents the page from navigating away (e.g. clicking a link to another site) once it has loaded. Defaults to false.

allowSelfSignedCertificates.description: Only relevant if htmlContent links to a remote https:// resource with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false.

clearCookies.description: Deletes all browser cookies before loading htmlContent. Defaults to false.

autoHeight.description: Automatically resizes the palette's height to fit the page content as it changes. Defaults to false.

uiId.description: The window to use, as returned by ShowScriptUI (1 to 8). Takes precedence over scriptId.

scriptId.description: Any text that identifies the calling script, so it uses its own window: ShowScriptUI gives a script without a window a free one, preferring the closed windows. The Tapir palette gives each script it starts its own id in the TAPIR_SCRIPT_ID environment variable, which aclib passes here automatically; that script's window is titled with its name and is freed when it ends. Without uiId and scriptId the first window is used.

SkylightAnchorPoint.description: Which point of the skylight anchorPosition places (API_SkylightType::anchorPoint).

SkylightData.description: The parameters of the new Skylight. The settings not given are the Skylight tool defaults' or the favorite's.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Skylight favorite to base the new element on.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

ownerId.description: The roof (single- or multi-plane) or shell the skylight is placed in.

libraryPartName.description: Optional localized name of a skylight library part to place instead of the tool default's.

anchorPosition.description: Global XY coordinates of the skylight's anchor point (API_SkylightType::anchorPosition). Archicad places the skylight on its owner roof or shell at this point; moving it onto another plane of a multi-plane roof has not been verified.

azimuthAngle.description: Rotation angle of the skylight in the horizontal plane, measured clockwise, in radians (API_SkylightType::azimuthAngle).

elevationAngle.description: Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians (API_SkylightType::elevationAngle). Archicad may set it again from the owner roof or shell.

pen.description: Pen of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the skylight.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the skylight; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines.

belowViewLinePen.description: Pen of the uncut lines of the skylight.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines.

surfaceId.description: Surface of the skylight (API_OpeningBaseType::mat); used unless useObjectMaterials is true.

useObjectPens.description: Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.

useObjectLineTypes.description: Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.

useObjectMaterials.description: Use the surfaces defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.

useObjectSectionAttributes.description: Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

SkylightDetails.description: The details of a Skylight: the settings CreateSkylights and ModifySkylights write, plus the library part, the owner and anchorLevel, which are only read.

anchorPosition.description: Global XY coordinates of the skylight's anchor point.

anchorPoint.description: Which point of the skylight anchorPosition places.

fixMode.description: What the skylight keeps when the angle or the height of its owner changes.

anchorLevel.description: The global Z coordinate of the anchor point. Only read; Archicad sets it from the owner.

azimuthAngle.description: Rotation angle in the horizontal plane, measured clockwise, in radians.

elevationAngle.description: Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians.

pen.description: Pen of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.

lineTypeId.description: Line type of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.

cutLineTypeId.description: Line type of the cut lines of the skylight.

sectionFillId.description: Fill of the section of the skylight; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the overhead lines.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type of the uncut lines.

surfaceId.description: Surface of the skylight; used unless useObjectMaterials is true.

SkylightFixMode.description: What the skylight keeps when the angle or the height of its owner changes (API_SkylightType::fixMode).

polygonOutline.description: The 2D coordinates of the outline of the hole, as Archicad returns them. The outline is closed implicitly (the first vertex is not repeated at the end); a curved edge is given by its end points only.

SlabData.description: The parameters of the new Slab.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

level.description: The Z coordinate value of the reference line of the slab.

thickness.description: Optional slab thickness. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType, buildingMaterialId or compositeId the new slab keeps the structure of the slab tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

structureType.description: Optional structure of the slab. If omitted, derived from buildingMaterialId or compositeId when one is given, otherwise the slab tool default (or the favorite) is kept.

buildingMaterialId.description: Building material of a Basic slab. Cannot be combined with compositeId.

compositeId.description: Composite attribute of a Composite slab. Cannot be combined with buildingMaterialId.

referencePlaneLocation.description: For a basic (homogeneous) slab only 'Top' or 'Bottom' are valid.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the edge of the slab.

polygonArcs.description: Polygon outline arcs of the slab.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

topMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the top of the slab.

sideMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the sides of the slab.

bottomMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the bottom of the slab.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

floorFill.description: The cover fill of the slab in the floor plan. Only the given fields change; of the orientation Archicad applies only its type through the API, read it back with GetDetailsOfElements.

level.description: Distance of the reference level of the slab from the floor level.

offsetFromTop.description: Vertical distance between the reference level and the top of the slab.

polygonArcs.description: Polygon outline arcs of the slab.

SlabQuantities.description: Quantities of a Slab element, as calculated by Archicad. Lengths in meters, areas in square meters, volumes in cubic meters.

volumeConditional.description: Conditional net volume of the slab.

topSurface.description: Net top surface of the slab.

bottomSurface.description: Net bottom surface of the slab.

edgeSurface.description: Net surface of the edges of the slab.

topSurfaceConditional.description: Conditional top surface of the slab.

bottomSurfaceConditional.description: Conditional bottom surface of the slab.

grossTopSurface.description: Gross top surface of the slab.

grossBottomSurface.description: Gross bottom surface of the slab.

grossEdgeSurface.description: Gross surface of the edges of the slab.

holesSurface.description: Total area of the holes in the slab.

holesPerimeter.description: Total perimeter of the holes in the slab.

SlabReferencePlaneLocation.description: Location of the slab reference plane.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the slab's reference level. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative level.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite slab first.

polygonOutline.description: Replaces the slab's entire polygon, including its holes - resend the holes field too to keep them, otherwise they are removed.

holes.description: Can be given on its own, without polygonOutline, to add/remove/clear holes in place (an empty array clears all holes) - the slab's current outline is reused unchanged.

topMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the top of the slab.

sideMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the sides of the slab.

bottomMaterial.description: Overrides the surface of the bottom of the slab.

cutFillPen.description: Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

cutFillBackgroundPen.description: Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.

floorFill.description: The cover fill of the slab in the floor plan. Only the given fields change; of the orientation Archicad applies only its type through the API, read it back with GetDetailsOfElements.

SnapFilter.description: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to while the designer clicks (Archicad's neig filter). Without it, the cursor snaps as usual.

base.description: What the cursor snaps to before include and exclude are applied: All = everything, None = nothing, Edges = only the lines and edges of the elements, Nodes = only their points (end points, vertices, hotspots). Default: None when include is given, otherwise All.

include.description: The cursor also snaps to these.

exclude.description: The cursor does not snap to these. Applied after include.

SnapType.description: A kind of point or line the cursor can snap to. An element type name means the element's points (end points, vertices, corners, hotspots); with On it means its lines and edges (for walls the reference line). Hotspot is a hotspot element, Text the corners of a text, Label the points of a label, Dimension a dimension point and DimensionOn the dimension line.

targetId.description: The element to be cut or modified.

SolidLinkFlags.description: Flags controlling the behaviour of a solid element operation link.

inheritOperatorAttributes.description: If true, the target element inherits the attributes of the operator element.

skipPolygonHoles.description: If true, holes of the operator (roof/slab) are ignored during the operation.

solidLinksWithTheGivenTarget.description: Links where the given element is the target (being cut or modified).

linkTime.description: When the solid link was made, as a date and time string formatted like the times of revision issues. Omitted when Archicad does not report it.

solidLinksWithTheGivenOperator.description: Links where the given element is the operator (performing the cut).

linkTime.description: When the solid link was made, as a date and time string formatted like the times of revision issues. Omitted when Archicad does not report it.

elements.description: The morphs created by the operation.

SolidOperationType.description: The type of solid element operation.

stairsData.description: Array of Stair data to check, with the same fields as the items of CreateStairs (without favoriteName). Nothing is created.

solutions.description: The results of the stair solver, aligned with the input stairsData.

path.description: The path of the special folder in the filesystem.

SpecialFolderPathOrError.description: The path of a special folder or an error.

SpecialFolderPathsOrErrors.description: A list of special folder paths or errors.

SpecialFolderType.description: The type of a special folder of the running Archicad.

SplineData.description: The parameters of the new Spline.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the spline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the spline points. Do not repeat the first point at the end even for a closed spline.

closed.description: Is this a closed curve? Optional, defaults to false.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.

lineTypeId.description: Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.

SplineDetails.description: Geometry of a Spline element. Geometry is read-only: Archicad's own API does not support modifying Spline geometry via ACAPI_Element_Change. The settings fields (roomSeparator/linePenIndex/lineTypeId) ARE modifiable via SET.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line?

elementId.description: A Spline element.

segmentIndex.description: The segment of the spline between its fit points segmentIndex and segmentIndex + 1, from 0 to the number of fit points - 2 (the fit points are the coordinates GetDetailsOfElements returns for the spline).

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates to measure from the segment.

maxDistance.description: The largest distance of the given coordinates from the spline segment.

SplineSettings.description: Settings for modifying a Spline. Only these settings fields are modifiable - Archicad's own API does not support changing Spline geometry (coordinates/closed) via ACAPI_Element_Change.

elements.description: The parts, first the original element, then the new ones (copies of it). A wall, beam or line gives two parts: the original keeps the part from its begin point to the split line. A slab, mesh or fill gives one part per piece of its polygon on each side of the line (more than two when the line crosses a concave polygon more than twice); the original keeps the largest. A polyline is cut at every crossing; the original keeps the part with its begin point.

The elements to split. Supported: straight walls (not polygonal, without doors, windows or openings), straight beams (not slanted or curved, one segment, without holes or openings), lines, slabs, meshes (without level lines or points), fills and polylines (one contour). Other types are reported with their type name.

line.description: The split line in project coordinates: the infinite line through begin and end, as the split line of Archicad's Split command.

results.description: One item per given element, in the same order.

StairBaselineData.description: The parameters of the Stair to check. Fields that are not given come from the current Stair tool defaults, as in CreateStairs.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates of the stair baseline polyline. Whether the baseline runs along the left edge, the right edge or the center of the flight is the Stair tool's baseline position, taken from the Stair tool defaults: with the baseline on the left edge, the flight lies to the right of it, looking from the first point to the last. The first point is kept; the length of the flight comes from the riser count and going, so the flight does not necessarily end at the last point given. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

finishVisible.description: Optional. If false, the tread/riser finishes are hidden and only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is modeled.

segmentType.description: Flight: steps. Landing: a landing segment, the edge between two landing turns of a U-shaped stair. DividedLanding: a divided landing segment.

baseLinePoints.description: The baseline polyline after the solver ran.

baseLineArcs.description: The arcs of the baseline after the solver ran, indexing baseLinePoints. Present only when the baseline has arcs.

totalHeight.description: Total height of the stair after the solver ran.

flightWidth.description: Width of the stair flight after the solver ran.

stepNum.description: Number of risers after the solver ran.

riserHeight.description: Height of each riser after the solver ran.

treadDepth.description: Depth (going) of each tread after the solver ran.

StairBaselineSolutionState.description: Correct: the baseline was already valid, nothing changed. Solved: the solver turned it into a valid baseline, returned in baseLinePoints. NotSolved: no valid baseline was found; CreateStairs is likely to fail or create an invalid stair with this input.

turnType.description: The turn at this point. The first and last points take None.

minLandingStartEdgeOffset.description: Optional, 0 by default. The minimal lead edge offset of a landing turn: makes the landing longer before the turn. Archicad calculates the actual offset, at least this much, to fit the steps (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as landingStartEdgeOffset).

minLandingEndEdgeOffset.description: Optional, 0 by default. The minimal trail edge offset of a landing turn: makes the landing longer after the turn. Archicad calculates the actual offset, at least this much (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as landingEndEdgeOffset).

landingStartEdgeOffset.description: The lead edge offset of the landing as Archicad calculated it.

landingEndEdgeOffset.description: The trail edge offset of the landing as Archicad calculated it.

StairData.description: The parameters of the new Stair.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates of the stair baseline polyline. Whether the baseline runs along the left edge, the right edge or the center of the flight is the Stair tool's baseline position, taken from baselinePosition, or else from the tool defaults or favoriteName: with the baseline on the left edge, the flight lies to the right of it, looking from the first point to the last. The first point is kept; the length of the flight comes from the riser count and going, so the flight does not necessarily end at the last point given. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

baselinePosition.description: Optional. Where the baseline runs on the flight, looking from the first point to the last. Left: along the left edge, the flight lies to the right of the baseline. Right: along the right edge, the flight lies to the left of it. Center: along the middle of the flight. Without it the baseline position of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is used.

baselineOffset.description: Optional. The offset of the baseline from the flight edge that baselinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center. Without it the offset of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is kept.

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

stepNum.description: Number of risers (steps). Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not have this many risers.

riserHeight.description: Height of each riser. Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not use this riser height.

treadDepth.description: Depth (going) of each tread. Pinned as a fixed going in the stair rules, so the run length follows from the number of treads; the standard's combined riser/going rules (2R+G, R+G, R/G) are not applied to this stair.

baseLineEdges.description: Optional. The segment type of each baseline edge, one item per edge (baseLinePoints.length - 1 items; edge i runs from point i to point i + 1). A U-shaped stair with a half landing is Flight, Landing, Flight with landing turns at both inner points. When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineVertices is given, every edge is a flight. Combinations Archicad cannot build fail like any other invalid stair.

baseLineVertices.description: Optional. The turn at each baseline point, one item per point (baseLinePoints.length items). When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineEdges is given, the first and last points get no turn and every other point a landing turn. Winders use Archicad's default winder settings.

treadDepthLocked.description: Whether the going lengths are locked.

totalHeightLocked.description: Whether the total height is locked.

finishVisible.description: Whether the tread and riser finishes of the stair are shown; false models only the structure (e.g. a monolith). The treads and risers of each part can also be switched on and off with treads and risers.

extraTopTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top.

extraBottomTread.description: Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom.

walkingLinePosition.description: Where the walking line runs on the flight: offset from the left or the right side (walkingLineOffset), centered, or placed by Archicad (Auto).

walkingLineOffset.description: The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center and Auto.

numberingType.description: Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers.

inputDirection.description: The walking direction along the baseline: upward from its first point, or inverse (downward).

uniformFinish.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.

uniformMonolithAttributes.description: Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.

uniformDrainings.description: Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.

structureVisibility.description: Whether the structure of the stair is shown.

treads.description: The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

risers.description: The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed.

structures.description: The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side: the left and right side structures and the structure under the stair. Only the given fields of the given parts and sides are changed.

StairDetails.description: The settings of a Stair element: the ones CreateStairs takes, and its floor plan and section display (stairDisplayType and the fields after it), which no command writes yet. The finishes and the structure are modeled by the Stair's subelements (risers, treads and structures), which GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists.

treadDepth.description: The tread depth (going) stored in the Stair's settings. Archicad does not keep it in step with the modeled treads: a placed stair can read 0 or 1 here, so take the modeled going from the geometry of its treads or risers (Get3DGeometryOfElements) instead.

level.description: Height of the stair base above the home story level.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute elevation of the stair base.

finishVisible.description: Whether the tread/riser finishes are modeled. If false only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is.

baseLinePoints.description: The baseline polyline the stair is placed along, in model coordinates, as given to CreateStairs.

baseLineArcs.description: The curved segments of the baseline, present only when it has any.

baseLineEdges.description: The segment type of each baseline edge, one item per edge (edge i runs from baseLinePoints[i] to baseLinePoints[i + 1]), as CreateStairs takes them.

baseLineVertices.description: The turn at each baseline point, one item per point, as CreateStairs takes them. A stair whose turns Archicad decided itself reports Landing at every point, also at the first and last.

stairDisplayType.description: Whether the floor plan display of the stair is set in the stair itself (Custom) or comes from the Model View Options (ByModelViewOptions) (API_StairType::stairDisplayType).

floorPlanLayout.description: The floor plan display of the stair's components (API_StairType::fpdLayout).

reflectedCeilingPlanLayout.description: The reflected ceiling plan display of the stair's components (API_StairType::rcpdLayout).

structureVisibility.description: Whether the structure of the stair is shown on the floor plan (API_StairType::structureVisibility).

structureSymbols.description: The symbol lines and fills of the stair's structure, one item per structure type and view (API_StairType::structSymbData).

visibleLineTypeId.description: Line type of the visible structure lines; left out when not set.

hiddenLineTypeId.description: Line type of the hidden structure lines; left out when not set.

visibleFillId.description: Fill type of the visible structure; left out when not set.

hiddenFillId.description: Fill type of the hidden structure; left out when not set.

monolithStructureSymbols.description: The symbol lines and fills of a monolithic structure, one item per view and visible or hidden part (API_StairType::monolithStructureSymbolData).

structureVisibilityOnStories.description: Which structure symbols are shown on which of the stair's relevant stories, one item per view (API_StairType::structureVisibilityOnStories).

stories.description: One item per story range relative to the stair's relevant stories (API_StairStructSymbRelevantStoriesID).

structures.description: Whether the lines of each structure are shown, per visible or hidden part.

fills.description: Whether the fills of each structure type are shown, per visible or hidden part.

monolithParts.description: Which parts of a monolithic structure are shown, per visible or hidden part.

StairGridType.description: How a stair's symbol is drawn on a story (API_StairGridTypeID).

StairLayout.description: The floor plan or reflected ceiling plan display of a Stair's components (API_StairLayoutData).

gridTypeAbove.description: The symbol shown on the stories above the stair's relevant stories.

gridTypeTop.description: The symbol shown on the top relevant story.

gridTypeMiddle.description: The symbol shown on the middle relevant stories.

gridTypeBottom.description: The symbol shown on the bottom relevant story.

gridTypeBelow.description: The symbol shown on the stories below the stair's relevant stories.

breakLineAngle.description: The angle of the break line, used when breakLineAngleType is AngleToVertical or AngleToHorizontal.

breakLineAngleNumberOfGoings.description: The number of goings the break line crosses, used when breakLineAngleType is NumberOfGoings.

breakLineDistance.description: The gap of the break line.

upperBreakLineCustomPosition.description: The height of the upper break line, used when breakLinePositionType is CustomHeight.

lowerBreakLineCustomPosition.description: The height of the lower break line, used when breakLinePositionType is CustomHeight.

upperBreakLineNthRiserPosition.description: The riser of the upper break line, used when breakLinePositionType is AtNthRiser.

lowerBreakLineNthRiserPosition.description: The riser of the lower break line, used when breakLinePositionType is AtNthRiser.

overrideLineType.description: Whether lineTypeId overrides the line types of the stair's components.

lineTypeId.description: The override line type; left out when not set.

overridePen.description: Whether pen overrides the line pens of the stair's components.

overrideSymbolFill.description: Whether symbolFillId and its pens override the symbol fills of the stair's components.

symbolFillId.description: The override symbol fill type; left out when not set.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the risers.

crossSection.description: The cross section of the risers.

angle.description: The angle of a slanted riser in radians.

position.description: Whether the risers stand on the treads or behind them.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the risers.

crossSection.description: The cross section of the risers.

angle.description: The angle of a slanted riser in radians.

position.description: Whether the risers stand on the treads or behind them.

StairStoryVisibility.description: The stories the stair is shown on.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

bottomType.description: The shape of the underside of the structure.

horizontalThickness.description: The horizontal thickness of the structure.

StairStructureType.description: The type of the structure: side stringers, monolithic, beam supported or cantilevered.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

structureType.description: The type of the structure: side stringers, monolithic, beam supported or cantilevered.

bottomType.description: The shape of the underside of the structure.

horizontalThickness.description: The horizontal thickness of the structure.

StairSymbolPart.description: Whether a stair structure symbol setting is for the visible or the hidden part of the structure (API_StairStructSymbPartID).

StairSymbolView.description: The view a stair structure symbol setting belongs to (API_StairStructSymbViewID).

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the treads.

nosingType.description: Whether the nosing is given by its length (nosingValue) or by the slant of the riser (nosingSlant).

nosingSlant.description: The slant of the nosing in radians.

role.description: The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).

offset.description: The offset of the treads.

nosingType.description: Whether the nosing is given by its length (nosingValue) or by the slant of the riser (nosingSlant).

nosingSlant.description: The slant of the nosing in radians.

totalHeight.description: The height of the stair relative to its bottom.

treadDepthLocked.description: Whether the going lengths are locked.
